bug_semantics: With authRequireGuestsToLogin enabled, OliveTin still lets an unauthenticated guest terminate another user's running action through KillAction. KillAction authenticates the caller (guest) and authorizes only via acl.IsAllowedKill; it never applies the dashboard guest-login gate. sanitizeAuthRequireGuestsToLogin forces DefaultPermissions.View/Exec/Logs to false but left DefaultPermissions.Kill at its constructor default true, so a guest with no matching ACL falls through aclCheck to defaultValue=true and can kill any live executionTrackingId.
flaw_origin: Kill permission was added in PR #618 as a default-true bit matching View/Exec/Logs and KillAction was wired to IsAllowedKill, but sanitizeAuthRequireGuestsToLogin was not extended to clear Kill. The first public write of config.DefaultPermissions.Kill = true is PR member 7cd67fc4ce4517517cba24308f3945aa032c5713 (parent lacks that assignment; Go zero-value false would have denied guests). That tree squash-landed on main as a8ac719af7da040e1ee26515cf7e876b65ff5a25. The GHSA/CVE fix is the missing sanitizer line, not an AI-attributed first-write.
